subject: Spatial and multilevel model with kriging/interpolation with R-INLA

messages.author: e0b2f531e15138b0
messages.subject: Spatial and multilevel model with kriging/interpolation with R-INLA
parts:
Dear R-INLA Group,
Please, I wish to analyse a spatial data using R-INLA  through multilevel approach with my main primary objective been to interpolate for observed/unobserved locations in my study region (using joint Gaussian distribution) and plotting the predicted values with their prediction variances/standard errors on a grid. 
Children in my data set are nested within households in the study locations and my multilevel model (without spatial) showed significant household random effects hence my choice to employ spatial analysis with multilevel approach. 
The need to include household random effects in my spatial model makes it a bit difficult for me to implement in R unlike the standard geostatistical analysis. 
I have a data frame containing my geographical coordinates (x=longitude and y=latitude) as well as my response and covariates.  
The spatial mixed effects model I wish to fit and interpolate is: Yij(t) = Xij(t)β +hj+S(t)+Ɛij           (1)
where i=individual child, j=household, X(t)= spatial referenced non-random covariates, S(t)= spatially correlated stationary Gaussian process. 
Ɛij =nugget effect/measurement error, Yij(t) = response of child i in household j at location t and my response is a continuous variable, hj =household level random effects and β=regression coefficients (spatial trend parameter). 
Specifically, S(t)~N(0,σ2H11(ɸ) ), where σ2  is the variance (partial sill),  H11(ɸ) is the correlation matrix based on valid correlation function h(u; ɸ), where u is the distance between locations and ɸ is the correlation parameter (range).
hj~N(0, σ2h), where σ2h is the household level variance (ie, hj is normally distributed with zero mean and variance σ2h). 
Ɛij~N(0,τ2), where τ2 is the nugget effect/measurement error (ie, Ɛij is normally distributed with zero mean and variance τ2). 

I am trying to achieve the above task through geostatistical analysis but other methods which can be implemented in R are also welcomed.

Please, could somebody help me with some papers in the literature, existing R code in R-INLA which are related to my problem as well as providing me with R codes to implement this assuming someone has already done this kind of multilevel spatial regression and interpolation in R. 
For the purpose of reproducibility, I have attached my data frame (d1.RData) as described above for any help. My outcome variable in the dataset is haz2 and is continuous, my covariates of interest are m5newf, v445new, hw1new, v012, v190newf, b0new, v481new and m18new. The household identifier is hhid and my spatial coordinates are x and y for longitude and latitude respectively. 

Many thanks for your help in advance. 

Justice
